The paper was published as a NASA Technical Memorandum in 2007.
The research was conducted at the NASA Glenn Research Center.
The paper was presented at the Turbo Expo 2006 conference organized by the American Society of Mechanical Engineers.
The experimental data used in the analysis was provided by Dr. Tony Arts and Dr. Karen Thole.
Thermal barrier coatings are a protective layer applied to turbine blades to insulate them from high temperatures.
The use of thermal barrier coatings reduces the heat transfer to the turbine blades.
The reduced heat transfer changes the cooling requirements for the turbine blades.
The paper discusses various turbine blade cooling approaches, including internal cooling channels, film cooling, and impingement cooling.
The presence of thermal barrier coatings affects the design and effectiveness of these different cooling methods.
The paper does not present any new experimental results, but rather analyzes the effects of thermal barrier coatings on turbine blade cooling approaches.
The paper is a review and analysis of the topic, rather than a report of original research findings.
The introduction provides an overview of the different types of NASA STI reports, including technical publications, technical memoranda, and contractor reports.
The paper acknowledges that understanding the effects of thermal barrier coatings on turbine blade cooling is important for the design and optimization of turbine engines.
The paper does not explicitly discuss the specific technical challenges or trade-offs involved in designing turbine blade cooling systems with thermal barrier coatings.
The paper suggests that the reduced heat transfer due to thermal barrier coatings requires a careful redesign of the cooling system to maintain effective cooling of the turbine blades.
